messages:
Anya: quick thought — we've got two competing proposals for internal API: 1) proto-first gRPC everywhere (typed, efficient) 2) JSON-over-http at the edge with proto/gRPC inside (gateway translation). I worry about loss of observability fidelity and error model mapping when we translate. Any strong opinions?

Mike C: I lean gateway+json at edge for client ergonomics and retry/backoff simplicity. But we need clear mapping for error codes and per-route quotas. today our quota metrics are attached to gRPC status codes and method names.

Sam G: +1 for gateway for customer facing SDKs. But we should keep a 'route id' header and propagate it. Then the runtime can emit metrics keyed by route id independent of transport.

Lee: agree with Sam. Also need to define canonical error shapes. If gateway maps a proto NOT_FOUND to 200+error-body that's dangerous. We should keep status mapping consistent.

Carol: telemetry ask: if we translate, instrument the gateway to emit both 'edge_latency' and 'backend_latency', and attach proto method name as attribute. That lets console show tail vs total.

Anya: good point — console needs to show rollout split signals (A/B) and per-model/quota impact. If gateway masks method names, rollout UX in console breaks.

Mike C: small proposal: gateway keeps 'x-rd-proto-method' header with original method, and 'x-rd-route-id'. Also preserve gRPC status in 'x-rd-grpc-status' when translating.

Sam G: +1. We should standardize a minimal header set. Draft:

```
x-rd-route-id: inference.text.generate-v2
x-rd-proto-method: /inference.v1.Inference/Generate
x-rd-grpc-status: 0
```

Lee: Also make sure quota enforcement can run in both gateway and backend. For low-latency customers we want gateway-local fast path (token bucket) and backend authoritative counters.

Carol: For metrics, backend should emit histogram: token_count_per_request, kv_cache_hit (0/1), backend_time_ms. Gateway should emit overall_time_ms, queue_time_ms.

Anya: rollout signal question: where do we store canary weights? console vs runtime? I prefer runtime-controlled weights with console UI just writing to config that the control plane picks up.

Mike C: agreed. console write -> control-plane versioned config -> runtime picks up atomically. Avoid racey UI-only flags.

deploy-bot: deploy started: gateway/proxy v1.12 -> canary subset 5% (config id: rc-20231122-gw)

Sam G: one more ops wrinkle: error grouping. Gateway should forward/annotate backend error fingerprint but not swallow stack traces. Minimal mapping:

- keep code
- map message
- keep debug_id header for support

Lee: final note: if we go proto at edge later, this header scheme still works. So it's backwards-compatible.

Anya: thanks all. I'll write a short RFC snippet and add header + metric checklist. Anyone want to take ownership of validating telemetry dashboards? cc @Carol

Carol: I'll own dashboards. I'll include the histograms and tag keys we've discussed.

Mike C: I can draft the gateway header shim and tests.

Anya: perfect. I'll create the RFC and link it here when ready. :+1:
